Steps: 1) Google Cloud project -> enable 'Blogger API v3'. 2) OAuth consent screen -> add scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/blogger. 3) Create an OAuth client (Desktop or Web). 4) Run the consent flow as the account that owns the blog; keep the REFRESH token. 5) Give us: oauth_token + blog_id (the long number in the Blogger dashboard URL).
Watch out for: THE BIG ONE. While the consent screen is in 'Testing', Google expires the refresh token after 7 DAYS - publishing silently dies every week. Moving the app to 'Production' requires Google verification. Budget for that review, or accept re-authorising every client weekly. We hold app client_id/secret already; what is missing is a per-blog token.

Steps: 1) Register an application (a valid OAuth2 redirect URL is required). 2) Note consumer key + secret. 3) Authorise as the client's Tumblr account with scopes: basic write offline_access. 4) Give us: oauth_token + blog (e.g. clientblog.tumblr.com).
Watch out for: Request 'offline_access' or the token cannot be refreshed and posting stops when it expires. Tumblr's API License also requires a per-post human action, which our approval step already satisfies.

Steps: 1) Create an application (any title; set a Redirect URL you control). 2) Note the client_id + client_secret. 3) Run the OAuth2 authorize flow SIGNED IN AS THE CLIENT'S WordPress.com account, approving the target blog. 4) Exchange the code for an access_token. 5) Give us: oauth_token + site (the blog's slug, e.g. clientname.wordpress.com).
Watch out for: The token is minted for the account that approves it, so the CLIENT (or you acting on a blog you created for them) must complete the consent step - the app credentials alone cannot post.

Steps: 1) Create a fine-grained PAT scoped to the client's repo with Contents: Read+Write and Pages: Read+Write. 2) Create the repo and enable Pages if it does not exist. 3) Give us: token + owner + repo.
Watch out for: We hold a token already; owner + repo are missing, so nothing can publish yet.

Steps: 1) Create a PAT with the 'api' scope. 2) Take the numeric Project ID from the project's home page. 3) Give us: token + project_id.
Watch out for: Pages only appear after CI runs, so a placement is not live the instant the API accepts it. We hold a token; project_id is missing.

Steps: Account -> Applications -> Create personal token. Give us: token.
Watch out for: As with Zenodo: a published item is permanent and citable.

Account needed: One account per CLIENT (or the client's institution)
Steps: Create a personal access token with deposit:write (and deposit:actions). Give us: access_token.
Watch out for: A Zenodo record is a permanent, citable research artefact with a DOI - it cannot be quietly deleted later. Only use it for clients with genuine research or data output.

Steps: 1) Settings -> Applications -> Generate a token with repository write access. 2) Create the 'pages' repo for the client. 3) Give us: token + owner + repo.
Settings -> API -> create an API token. Give us: token.
1) Create the site (free tier is fine: 1 GB, 200 GB/month). 2) Settings -> Manage Site Settings -> API key. 3) Give us: api_key.
1) User settings -> Applications -> New access token. 2) Create the site (or take an existing one) and copy its Site ID from Site configuration. 3) Give us: token + site_id.
Settings -> Personal access tokens -> create with osf.full_write. Give us: token.
Watch out for: Academic-integrity norms apply; only for genuinely research-adjacent clients.

Cost: Free during the public alpha for basic publishing
Steps: Generate a personal access token. Give us: token + the site domain.
Watch out for: Publishing via the BUILD system needs a paid sourcehut account; the direct tarball upload we use does not. Treat the free path as alpha-grade.

Steps: Nothing to fetch. Run: python -m app.cli.web2_signup --platforms 'Telegra.ph' then register the printed credential with app.cli.web2_accounts.
Watch out for: Zero identity means low trust and low link value. Use it for reach, not authority.

Steps: Create a token with Gists: Read+Write. Give us: token.
Watch out for: Gist links are nofollow - useful for reach, not for link equity.

Steps: Create a PAT with the 'api' scope. Give us: token.
Watch out for: Snippet links are nofollow.

Cost: PAID - Hashnode Pro, $5 per seat / month
Steps: 1) Settings -> Developer -> generate a Personal Access Token. 2) Take the publication id from the dashboard URL (hashnode.com/dashboards/<PUBLICATION_ID>/general). 3) Give us: pat + publication_id.
Watch out for: As of 13 May 2026 BOTH read and publish access to Hashnode's GraphQL API require a Pro subscription. A token issued on a free account will be rejected. Do not assign this until someone decides to pay.

Steps: Settings -> Extensions -> 'DEV Community API Keys' -> generate. Give us: api_key.
Watch out for: Links are nofollow and dev.to's rules forbid off-topic promotional posts - only genuinely developer-audience clients belong here.
